description.content: Manage project reports in your account
This API is used for creating a site report aka project report based on a report template.
Added as a part of security scheme: apikey

This API returns all Project Reports aka project reports of a specfic project based on its id. Without any extra parameters it will return the first 100 reports ordered by ascending ID. Extra parameters can be added to sort the results. The sort is always ascending unless the field name is prefixed with a minus (U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, "-") i.e. `-id` or `id`.
Report Sorting: Reports can be sorted by id: sequential-id, name: title, template: site-report-template-id, status: status, author: user-id, creation date: created-at, update date: updated-at.
Example#1: `/site_reports?sort=-sequential-id`
Example#2: `/site_reports?sort=created-at`

query.description: search keyword based on which reports are returned
sets the number of pages for the returned reports

sets the number of reports that should be returned per page
Maximum is 500, default is 100

This API is used for exporting one or multiple project reports as an Excel file. It takes the id/s of the report/s and exports it/them.
Example: export_reports?ids[]=wjb&ids[]=nak
Reports can be sorted before being exported. They can be sorted by id: sequential-id, name: title, template: site-report-template-id, status: status, author: user-id, creation date: created-at and update date: updated-at. The sort is always ascending unless the field name is prefixed with a minus (U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, "-") i.e. `-id` or `id.
Example: export_reports?ids[]=wjb&ids[]=nak&ids[]=pxq&sort=title
It is also possible to export reports filtered by the template-id of one of the customer's created templates or by a searched keyword. Therefore you have to set the project_id to 0.
Example: export_reports?search=template&filter[template_id]=ojk

Example: download_combined_reports?ids[]=jdg&ids[]=pxq&sort=status
It is also possible to export reports filtered by the template-id of one of the customer's created templates or by a searched keyword. Therefore you have to set the project_id to 0.
Example: download_combined_reports?search=template&filter[template_id]=ojk

description.content:
Welcome to PlanRadar's API documentation, here you can find all the details about our APIs as well as test them online.
Rate Limits
30 requests per minute per account, aggregated across all tokens.
If the threshold is exceeded, a 5-minute cooldown is applied to the account, aggregated across all tokens.
During the cooldown period, further requests may be rejected until the cooldown ends.
In rare cases, an endpoint may have a different rate limit than the default. When that happens, the differing limit will be explicitly stated in the API documentation for that endpoint.
Access Key
In order to be able to access any API you have to create an access token.Therefore you have to follow these steps:-
  • Go to your profile page and click on Personal Access Tokens on the left side bar
  • Click on the 'Create Access Token' top right button in order to create a new access token.
  • Copy the created token and paste it into the field that pops up when you click on the 'Authorize' button
  • Note: you can copy the token only once.
  • Now you can easily access any API
V2 APIs
We are currently working on upgrading all our APIs to v2, and we recommend that you use v2 APIs if it is available.

V2 APIs are faster, robust and more flexible than v1 APIs
